summary: The last standing lookout on the Sandpoint Ranger District, Lunch Peak's 1971 cab was wrapped to survive the 2021 Trestle Creek fire and is now a rental.

access.note: Forest Service recreation rental (recreation.gov); last 4 miles of access road rough, high-clearance recommended.

visit.trail_note: Pend Oreille Divide Trail #67 starts just below the lookout; rental cabin.

events.note: First lookout: 45-foot pole tower with L-4 cab.
Current 15x15-ft flattop/R-6 cab on 10-ft concrete base built.
Trestle Creek Complex fire nearby; crew wrapped the lookout in protective material due to local concern it could be lost.

evidence.supports: location, elevation, 2002 remodel, current rental amenities, access road
evidence.quote: The 15'x15' cabin was remodeled in 2002 and sits atop a 15' high cinder block foundation. No water or heat is provided... The last four miles of the access road is rough in spots and high clearance vehicles are necessary.

evidence.supports: 1937 first lookout, 1971 current structure, last modern lookout on district
evidence.quote: The first lookout on the site was a hip roof L-4 cab on a 50' pole tower built in 1937. In 1971 the current 15'x15' flattop cab with catwalk on a 10' concrete base was constructed and remained in service until 1985.

evidence.supports: 1937 pole tower, 1971 R-6 cab, last staffed 1985, staff name Harold Harding
evidence.quote: A 45' pole tower with L-4 cab was built here in 1937. The present 10' concrete base with R-6 flat cab was constructed in 1971, and was last staffed full-time in 1985.

evidence.supports: 2021 Trestle Creek fire wrapping, staff names Harding/Young
evidence.quote: Summer fire season 2021 the Trestle Creek fire – the tower was wrapped due to overwhelming concern from local citizens.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says 50-ft pole tower; firelookout.com says 45-ft. Story states both figures and attributes each to its source rather than asserting a single unresolved number; design cab type (L-4) agreed.

notes_for_editor: Minor conflict on pole-tower height of the 1937 structure (45 vs 50 ft); both figures are now attributed to their sources in the narrative rather than stated as a single number. Elevation conflicts slightly between brief (1907.4m) and rec.gov (6,414 ft = 1955m) but not asserted as a specific figure in the story. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): draft had stated the pole height as a flat '45-foot' figure sourced to both NHLR and firelookout.com, but NHLR actually gives 50 feet, contradicting its own citation -- fixed to attribute each figure correctly. Draft also said staffer Diane Young served 'around 1970'; idahofirelookouts.com's staff list actually dates her 1975-1978 -- fixed.
